The only raw quantity involved is `stimOn_times`, which defines where the grid is placed; the values themselves are definitional. The AI unit-tested the vector in step 97, printing `[-0.49 -0.47 -0.45] ... [1.45 1.47 1.49]` to confirm the endpoints.\n\n## 3-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Time since stimulus onset*?\n\ni. None beyond constructing the bin-centre vector and broadcasting it across trials into `inputs[:, 0, :]` as `float32`. The instructions asked for a continuous, time-varying input, so it is left as a real-valued ramp rather than a binary onset indicator.\n\nii.\n```python\nn_trials = int(keep.sum())\ninputs = np.empty((n_trials, 2, N_BINS), dtype=np.float32)\ninputs[:, 0, :] = bin_centres[None, :]\ninputs[:, 1, :] = n_in_block[:, None]\n```\n\niii. A comment states the choice: \"Time since stimulus onset at the centre of each neural bin.\" The centre rather than an edge is chosen so the input labels the instant the bin represents; the AI notes the distinction from the behaviour sampling (right edge) explicitly in `alignment_note`.\n\n## 3-c. How is the `input` *Time since stimulus onset* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. By construction: bin *i* of the neural array covers `[stimOn - 0.5 + 0.02i, stimOn - 0.5 + 0.02(i+1))`, and `inputs[:, 0, i]` is the centre of that same bin. The two share the same index axis and the same origin, so column *i* of `neural` and column *i* of `input` describe the same 20 ms of the same trial. Both arrays are length 100 for all trials, which the verifier confirmed (`T: min 100, max 100`).\n\nii.\n```python\nb = np.floor((t - interval_begs[k]) / BINSIZE).astype(np.int64)   # neural grid\nbin_centres = TIME_WINDOW[0] + (np.arange(N_BINS) + 0.5) * BINSIZE  # input = centres of that grid\n```\n\niii. Recorded in `alignment_note`: \"Neural bin i spans [stimOn - 0.5 + 0.02*i, stimOn - 0.5 + 0.02*(i+1)). time_from_stimulus_onset is the centre of that bin\". No further alignment is needed because both derive from the same `interval_begs`.\n\n## 4-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Trial number in block* derived from?\n\ni. From `trials['probabilityLeft']` alone. The IBL trials table carries no block identifier, so blocks are recovered as maximal runs of constant `probabilityLeft`; a change of value starts a new block.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef trial_number_in_block(trials):\n    p_left = trials['probabilityLeft'].to_numpy(dtype=float)\n    # NaN != NaN, so a NaN run is broken up; that is fine, those trials are excluded.\n    new_block = np.ones(len(p_left), dtype=bool)\n    new_block[1:] = ~(p_left[1:] == p_left[:-1])\n    block_id = np.cumsum(new_block) - 1\n```\n\niii. The AI knew from the papers (and states in `task_description`) that \"After 90 unbiased trials (p(left) = 0.5) the stimulus side is drawn in blocks of 20-100 trials with p(left) = 0.2 or 0.8; block switches are uncued\" — so `probabilityLeft` is piecewise constant and fully determines the block boundaries. The NaN case is handled deliberately (a NaN run splits blocks, but those trials are excluded anyway).\n\n## 4-b. What processing is involved in computing `input` *Trial number in block*?\n\ni. A 0-based counter of the trial's position within its block, computed on the **full** trials table before any trial is excluded, then subsampled with `keep` — so a trial dropped by QC still advances the counter and the value reflects the animal's real position in the block. Stored as `float32`, constant across the 100 bins of a trial.\n\n**Caveat found in the trajectory:** the first implementation of the offset lookup was wrong — it prepended a 0 and indexed `block_id` into the shifted array, so every block after the first was offset by the *previous* block's start. The AI unit-tested it at step 97 on `[0.5]*4 + [0.2]*3 + [0.8]*2 + [0.2]*1` and got `[0 1 2 3 4 5 6 3 4 2]` instead of `[0 1 2 3 0 1 2 0 1 0]`, said \"Found a bug in the block-index helper\", and fixed it at step 101. **The fix landed after the full conversion had already been written** (`converted_data.pkl` 23:51, `convert_data.py` 23:57) and the pickle was never regenerated, so the shipped data carries the buggy values. The verifier output on the shipped pickle confirms it: `trial_number_in_block: [0.0, 178.0]`, whereas the largest IBL block is ~100 trials (the expert file tops out at 98).\n\nii. Shipped code (fixed):\n```python\n    block_id = np.cumsum(new_block) - 1\n    block_start = np.flatnonzero(new_block)\n    idx_in_block = np.arange(len(p_left)) - block_start[block_id]\n    return idx_in_block.astype(np.float32)\n```\n\nBuggy version used for `converted_data.pkl`:\n```python\n    block_id = np.cumsum(new_block) - 1\n    idx_in_block = np.arange(len(p_left)) - np.concatenate(\n        [[0], np.flatnonzero(new_block)])[block_id]\n    return idx_in_block.astype(np.float32)\n```\n\nWhere it is applied:\n```python\nn_in_block = trial_number_in_block(trials)[keep]\n...\ninputs[:, 1, :] = n_in_block[:, None]\n```\n\niii. Docstring: \"0-based index of each trial within its block of constant probabilityLeft. Computed on the *full* trials table, before any trial is excluded, so that the value reflects the animal's actual position in the block rather than a position in the filtered sequence.\" The AI caught the arithmetic error itself via a hand-built unit test but ran out of runway to re-run the 5.5-minute conversion (its attempts to free the GPU by killing the training job at steps 100/102 failed, and the session ended).\n\n## 5-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Choice* derived from?\n\ni. The single column `trials['choice']`, which is IBL-coded +1 / -1 / 0.\n\nii.\n```python\n# IBL codes choice as +1 when the mouse reported the stimulus on the LEFT\n# (verified: trials with contrastLeft > 0 and feedbackType == +1 all have\n# choice == +1) and -1 for a right report. The task asks for left = 0, right = 1.\nchoice = (trials['choice'].to_numpy()[keep] == -1).astype(np.int64)\n```\n\niii. The AI did not take the sign convention on faith. At steps 56–57 it loaded a trials table and cross-checked `choice` against `contrastLeft`/`feedbackType`, and recorded the result in the comment quoted above: trials with a left stimulus and positive feedback all have `choice == +1`, so +1 is a leftward report.\n\n## 5-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Choice*?\n\ni. A single recode: `choice == -1 → 1` (right), everything else → 0 (left). No-response trials (`choice == 0`) cannot reach this line because the trial mask already removed them, so the `else` branch only ever sees +1. The scalar is broadcast across all 100 bins so the output is time-varying in shape, and `output_values[0] = ['left', 'right']`. Observed split 0.508 / 0.492.\n\nii.\n```python\noutputs = np.empty((n_trials, 4, N_BINS), dtype=np.int64)\noutputs[:, 0, :] = choice[:, None]\n```\n\niii. The instructions specify \"Choice, binary, per-trial, left = 0, right = 1\", and the format spec says \"If at all possible, make it time-varying\" — hence the broadcast to a constant time series rather than a bare scalar.\n\n## 6-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Prior probability of left* derived from?\n\ni. `trials['probabilityLeft']`, the block prior held constant within a block.\n\nii.\n```python\np_left_all = trials['probabilityLeft'].to_numpy(dtype=float)\nprior_all = np.full(len(trials), -1, dtype=np.int64)\nfor value, code in ((0.2, 0), (0.5, 1), (0.8, 2)):\n    prior_all[np.isclose(p_left_all, value)] = code\n```\n\niii. Directly from the instructions (\"Prior probability of left, per-trial, 0.2 -> 0, 0.5 -> 1, 0.8 -> 2\"). This is the same column that defines the block structure used for input 2, so the two are consistent by construction.\n\n## 6-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Prior probability of left*?\n\ni. Recode 0.2/0.5/0.8 → 0/1/2 using `np.isclose` (float tolerance rather than exact equality), initialising to a `-1` sentinel; any trial still at -1 is excluded by `keep &= (prior_all >= 0)`, so an unexpected prior value drops the trial rather than silently mislabelling it. The code is broadcast across the 100 bins and labelled `['p_left=0.2', 'p_left=0.5', 'p_left=0.8']`. Observed fractions 0.417 / 0.141 / 0.442 — the 0.5 minority is the unbiased opening block, which is kept.\n\nii.\n```python\nkeep = trials_mask & np.isfinite(interval_begs_all) & (prior_all >= 0)\n...\nprior = prior_all[keep]\noutputs[:, 1, :] = prior[:, None]\n```\n\niii. Comment: \"Block identity, one of the three probabilities the task defines.\" The `-1` sentinel plus the `keep` gate is a defensive choice so that a value outside the three the task defines can never be encoded as a valid class. The unbiased block is kept because the reference's `load_trials_and_mask` is called with `exclude_unbiased=False` (its default).\n\n## 7-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Wheel speed* derived from?\n\ni. `sess_loader.wheel['times']` and `sess_loader.wheel['velocity']` from `SessionLoader.load_wheel()`, i.e. the wheel velocity that ibllib derives from `_ibl_wheel.position` / `_ibl_wheel.timestamps`. Speed is the absolute value of that velocity.\n\nii.\n```python\nsl = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\nsl.load_wheel()\ntraces['wheel-speed'] = (sl.wheel['times'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),\n                         np.abs(sl.wheel['velocity'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)))\n```\n\niii. Copied from the reference's `load_target_behavior(..., 'wheel-speed')`, which is `np.abs(sess_loader.wheel['velocity'].to_numpy())`. The docstring says so: \"Follows the reference `load_target_behavior` / `bin_behaviors`: wheel speed is the absolute value of the Gaussian-smoothed wheel velocity\". (Note the AI repeats the reference's own docstring wording \"Gaussian-smoothed\"; the current ibllib `load_wheel` interpolates position to 1 kHz and differentiates with a Butterworth low-pass.)\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Wheel speed*?\n\ni. Four steps: (1) `SessionLoader.load_wheel()` interpolates the (movement-triggered) wheel position onto a uniform grid and computes a smoothed velocity; (2) absolute value → speed in rad/s; (3) linear interpolation of that trace onto the 100 per-trial sample times; (4) discretisation into 3 per-session levels. The interpolation is fully vectorised across all trials at once via a single `np.interp` on a flattened `(n_trials, 100)` query matrix. `np.interp` clamps rather than extrapolates outside the trace, which is harmless because the coverage mask already guarantees samples within one bin of both window edges.\n\nii.\n```python\n    offsets = (np.arange(N_BINS) + 1) * BINSIZE\n    sample_times = interval_begs[:, None] + offsets[None, :]\n    binned = np.interp(sample_times.ravel(), times, values).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS)\n```\n\niii. Docstring of `bin_behaviour`: \"The sample time of bin i is `beg + (i+1) * BINSIZE`, i.e. the right edge of the bin, matching the reference `get_behavior_per_interval` (`x_interp = linspace(beg + binsize, end, n_bins)`).\" The AI read that function (step 13) and reproduced its grid exactly rather than choosing its own.\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Wheel speed* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Into 3 levels at the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles **of that session's own kept-trial values** (all trials × all bins pooled), via `np.digitize`. A degenerate trace (both quantiles equal) is nudged with `np.nextafter` so the bins stay ordered instead of collapsing. The two thresholds are stored per session in `metadata['session_info']`. Resulting marginals are 0.333 / 0.333 / 0.333.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretize_tertiles(values):\n    lo, hi = np.quantile(values, [1.0 / 3.0, 2.0 / 3.0])\n    if not hi > lo:  # degenerate (e.g. a mostly constant trace): keep bins ordered\n        hi = np.nextafter(lo, np.inf)\n    return np.digitize(values, [lo, hi]).astype(np.int64), (float(lo), float(hi))\n\nwheel_lvl, wheel_thr = discretize_tertiles(beh_binned['wheel-speed'][keep])\n```\n\niii. Argued at length in the docstring: \"Thresholds are the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles of that session's own values. Both behaviours are in arbitrary, session-dependent units … and wheel speed on how vigorously that mouse turns — so a global threshold would mostly encode which session a trial came from. Per-session tertiles make the three levels mean 'slow / medium / fast for this animal' in every session and keep the classes balanced, which is what the balanced-accuracy score the decoder is graded with assumes.\" The AI also inspected the empirical distributions of the behaviour traces (steps 59/61) before settling on tertiles.\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Wheel speed* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The same `interval_begs = stimOn_times - 0.5` origin and the same 20 ms grid as the spikes, so index *i* of the output matches index *i* of the neural matrix. The only difference is the sampling point within the bin: the wheel trace is evaluated at the **right edge** `beg + (i+1)*0.02`, whereas the neural bin *i* aggregates `[beg + i*0.02, beg + (i+1)*0.02)` and the time input is the bin centre — a 10 ms offset. The wheel is already on the session clock, so no extra clock alignment is needed.\n\nii.\n```python\n    interval_ends = interval_begs + N_BINS * BINSIZE\n    offsets = (np.arange(N_BINS) + 1) * BINSIZE\n    sample_times = interval_begs[:, None] + offsets[None, :]\n```\n\n```python\n'alignment_note': ('... wheel speed and whisker motion energy are linearly '\n                   'interpolated onto its right edge, as in the reference pipeline.'),\n```\n\niii. The offset is deliberate and documented in `alignment_note`: the AI chose fidelity to the reference's `x_interp = np.linspace(beg + binsize, end, n_bins)` over a bin-centre convention, and flagged the difference in the metadata so it is visible downstream.\n\n## 8-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Whisker motion energy* derived from?\n\ni. `sess_loader.motion_energy['leftCamera']['times']` and `['whiskerMotionEnergy']` from `SessionLoader.load_motion_energy(views=['left'])` — the IBL-released ROI motion energy over a whisker-pad bounding box. If the left camera fails to load, the right camera is used instead; if neither is available the whole session is dropped (13 of the 15 skipped sessions).\n\nii.\n```python\n    whisker = None\n    for view, cam in (('left', 'leftCamera'), ('right', 'rightCamera')):\n        try:\n            sl_me = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n            sl_me.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n            df = sl_me.motion_energy[cam]\n            whisker = (df['times'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),\n                       df['whiskerMotionEnergy'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64))\n            break\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n    if whisker is None:\n        raise RuntimeError('no whisker motion energy available')\n```\n\niii. This is the reference's own fallback in `bin_behaviors`: \"if beh == 'whisker-motion-energy': target_dict = load_target_behavior(one, eid, 'left-whisker-motion-energy'); if 'skip' in target_dict.keys(): … 'right-whisker-motion-energy'\". The method-paper excerpt the AI read defines the signal: \"Whisker motion energy is computed as the mean absolute difference between adjacent video frames within a bounding box anchored between nose tip and eye.\"\n\n## 8-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Whisker motion energy*?\n\ni. The released trace is used as-is — no filtering, normalisation or unit conversion. It goes through the identical `bin_behaviour` path as the wheel: linear interpolation onto the right edge of each of the 100 bins, a coverage/NaN mask, then per-session tertiles. Because left and right cameras run at different frame rates (60 vs 150 Hz), the interpolation is what puts both on a common grid.\n\nii.\n```python\nfor name, (t, v) in traces.items():\n    binned, good = bin_behaviour(t, v, safe_begs)\n    beh_binned[name] = binned\n    keep &= good\n```\n\niii. Same justification as the wheel — the AI treats both continuous behaviours through one function so their grid, coverage test and discretisation are guaranteed identical, and it notes the camera-rate dependence as one reason the thresholds must be per-session: \"whisker motion energy depends on the camera (left at 60 Hz vs right at 150 Hz), the illumination and the size of the bounding box\".\n\n## 8-c. How is `output` *Whisker motion energy* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. Identically to the wheel: 3 levels split at the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles of that session's own kept values, `np.digitize`, `np.nextafter` guard for degenerate traces, thresholds recorded in `session_info`, labels `['low', 'medium', 'high']`. Marginals 0.333 / 0.334 / 0.333.\n\nii.\n```python\nwhisk_lvl, whisk_thr = discretize_tertiles(beh_binned['whisker-motion-energy'][keep])\noutputs[:, 3, :] = whisk_lvl\n```\n\niii. See 7-c — the AI's argument is explicitly about *both* behaviours being in arbitrary session-dependent units, with the camera model/illumination/box size named as the specific confounds for motion energy.\n\n## 8-d. How is `output` *Whisker motion energy* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Same as the wheel: the camera frame times are on the shared session clock, and the trace is interpolated onto `stimOn_times - 0.5 + (i+1)*0.02` for i = 0..99, giving one value per neural bin at the bin's right edge. Trials whose window is not covered by the camera to within one bin at either end are dropped rather than extrapolated.\n\nii.\n```python\n    i0 = np.searchsorted(times, interval_begs, side='right')\n    i1 = np.searchsorted(times, interval_ends, side='left')\n    good = i1 > i0\n    good[idx] &= np.abs(interval_begs[idx] - times[i0[idx]]) <= BINSIZE\n    good[idx] &= np.abs(interval_ends[idx] - times[i1[idx] - 1]) <= BINSIZE\n```\n\niii. Same as 7-d; the coverage tolerance of one bin is the reference's (\"`np.abs(interval_begs[interval_idx] - target_time[0]) > binsize` → 'target data starts too late'\"), which the AI ported rather than inventing a tolerance.\n\n## 9. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Missing or malformed data is dropped at the narrowest level that still leaves the rest usable:\n- **Trial level:** NaN in any of the six required trial events; non-finite `stimOn`-derived window start; a `probabilityLeft` outside {0.2, 0.5, 0.8}; a wheel or camera trace that does not span the window or yields non-finite interpolated values.\n- **Probe level:** an insertion whose spike sorting is empty, or that contributes zero surviving clusters, is skipped and the session continues on its other probe.\n- **Spike level:** cluster ids out of range for the cluster table and non-finite spike times are discarded.\n- **Session level:** no surviving units → dropped; fewer than 2 usable trials → dropped; no whisker motion energy on either camera → dropped. Any unhandled exception in a worker is caught, recorded with its traceback, and that session alone is skipped so the run completes.\n- **Degenerate distributions:** a near-constant behavioural trace gets `hi = nextafter(lo)` so `digitize` still returns ordered classes.\n- **Bookkeeping:** every dropped session and its reason is written into `metadata['skipped_sessions']` (15 entries), and per-session trial counts before/after filtering are kept as `n_trials_recorded` / `n_trials`.\n\nii.\n```python\n        ok = (sc >= 0) & (sc < lut.size)\n        sc, st = sc[ok], st[ok]\n        mapped = lut[sc]\n        ok = mapped >= 0\n        # Spike times can contain NaN for samples outside the sync range.\n        ok &= np.isfinite(st)\n```\n\n```python\n    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - a bad session must not stop the run\n        return eid, None, f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\\n{traceback.format_exc()}'\n```\n\n```python\n'skipped_sessions': [{'eid': e, 'reason': str(m).splitlines()[0]}\n                     for e, m in sorted(skipped)],\n```\n\niii. The catch-all is justified inline (\"a bad session must not stop the run\") and paired with a full traceback so failures are diagnosable rather than silent. The AI also investigated rather than papered over an anomaly: 38 trials verify as all-zero neural data, and at steps 81–86 it traced one of them to a genuine gap in the spike record, concluding \"Spike gap is real data, not a bug\", and left those trials in.\n\n## 10-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. Dominated by I/O in `load_session_units`: `ssl.load_spike_sorting()` per probe, which reads the large `spikes.times`/`spikes.clusters` arrays (699 insertions over 459 sessions) and, because `check_hash` is left at its default, also re-reads each file to verify its md5. Two secondary costs: `load_spike_sorting` pulls the loader's full default `SPIKES_ATTRIBUTES` (`amps` and `depths` as well as `times` and `clusters`), roughly doubling the bytes read for arrays that are never used; and `SessionLoader` is constructed and made to load three separate times per session (trials, wheel, motion energy). Everything after loading is cheap — the per-trial spike-binning loop, and the behaviour interpolation which is a single vectorised `np.interp`. With 24 worker processes the whole 459-session run took 334 s wall-clock, and pickling the 11.73 GB result is itself a noticeable share of that.\n\nii.\n```python\n        ssl = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=str(row['pid']), one=one, eid=eid,\n                                 pname=row['probe_name'])\n        spikes, clusters, channels = ssl.load_spike_sorting()\n```\n\n```python\n    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:\n        futures = {pool.submit(_worker, task): task[0] for task in tasks}\n```\n\niii. The AI never states this in prose, but its design shows it identified I/O as the bottleneck: the whole conversion is process-parallel over sessions, and it pre-warms the Allen atlas in the parent with a comment — \"Make sure the Allen atlas files are cached before the workers start, otherwise every worker downloads them at once\" — i.e. it removed a known startup stampede. It measured single-session load times in steps 51–55 (\"test the full pipeline on one session to understand timing\") before choosing the worker count.\n\n## 10-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. Three:\n1. `bin_spikes`'s `for k in range(n_trials)` loop. It could be done in one pass by offsetting each spike's flat index by its trial (`trial * n_units * N_BINS + u * N_BINS + b`) and calling `bincount` once, since `searchsorted` has already located every trial's slice. As written it also builds a fresh `(n_units * N_BINS,)` count vector per trial.\n2. The per-probe loop in `load_session_units`. Genuinely sequential because each probe is a separate file read, so there is little to gain.\n3. The three list comprehensions that unpack the stacked `(n_trials, ...)` arrays into per-trial lists (`[binned_spikes[k] for k in range(n_trials)]` etc.). These are required by the target format, but they leave `n_trials` non-contiguous views alive per session, which inflates the pickle.\n\nNotably the behaviour path is *already* vectorised across trials — a single `np.interp` over a flattened query matrix, and a fully vectorised coverage mask — where the reference repo spawns a multiprocessing pool per behaviour per session.\n\nii.\n```python\n    for k in range(n_trials):\n        t = spike_times[i0[k]:i1[k]]\n        if t.size == 0:\n            continue\n        u = spike_units[i0[k]:i1[k]]\n        b = np.floor((t - interval_begs[k]) / BINSIZE).astype(np.int64)\n        np.clip(b, 0, N_BINS - 1, out=b)\n        counts = np.bincount(u * N_BINS + b, minlength=flat)\n        out[k] = counts.reshape(n_units, N_BINS)\n```\n\n```python\n    binned = np.interp(sample_times.ravel(), times, values).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS)\n```\n\niii. No explicit reasoning is given for leaving the spike loop scalar. The vectorisation of the behaviour path is implicitly justified by the AI having replaced the reference's nested-`multiprocessing` `get_behavior_per_interval` with plain NumPy — it already parallelises at the session level, so a second, inner pool would oversubscribe the machine.\n\n## 10-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. Four repetitions, all cheap-to-moderate:\n1. **`SessionLoader` is built and loaded three (sometimes four) times per session** — once in `load_trials_and_mask`, once in `load_behaviour_traces` for the wheel, and once per camera view tried. One loader instance can serve `load_trials()`, `load_wheel()` and `load_motion_energy()`; the reference repo does exactly that, and its `load_trials_and_mask` even accepts a `sess_loader` argument for this purpose.\n2. **`BrainRegions()` is instantiated once per session** inside `convert_session`, in addition to the one built in `main` to pre-warm the cache — so the atlas tables are re-parsed 459 times instead of once per worker.\n3. **`acronym2acronym(..., mapping='Beryl')` is applied to the whole cluster table per probe** and then indexed down to the kept clusters; mapping only the kept rows would do the same work on ~10% of the rows (though the mask depends on the mapping, so one pass is unavoidable).\n4. **Behaviour binning is computed for every trial in the session**, including trials the trials mask has already rejected (see 10-d).\n\nii.\n```python\n    sess_loader = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)     # in load_trials_and_mask\n    ...\n    sl = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid); sl.load_wheel()          # in load_behaviour_traces\n    ...\n        sl_me = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)                     # again, per camera view\n        sl_me.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n```\n\n```python\ndef convert_session(eid, probe_rows, subject, lab):\n    from iblatlas.regions import BrainRegions\n    one = get_one()\n    brain_regions = BrainRegions()      # rebuilt for every session\n```\n\niii. Not addressed in the trajectory. The repeated `SessionLoader` construction looks like a consequence of keeping `load_trials_and_mask` a faithful standalone re-implementation of the reference function (it creates its own loader, as the original does) rather than an oversight about cost; `get_one()` *is* memoised per process, so the expensive part (the ONE client and its cache tables) is shared.\n\n## 10-d. What unnecessary processing does the code do that is discarded in downstream analyses?\n\ni. Five items:\n1. **Behaviour is binned for all trials, then thrown away for most of them.** `bin_behaviour` is called on `safe_begs`, which spans the *entire* trials table, so wheel and whisker traces are interpolated onto 100 bins for every recorded trial; only the `keep` subset survives (`beh_binned[...][keep]`). Typically ~30–40% of the interpolation work is discarded. It also fabricates `safe_begs = 0.0` windows for NaN-`stimOn` trials purely so the array shapes line up, then interpolates those too.\n2. **Unused spike attributes are read from disk.** `load_spike_sorting()` fetches `amps` and `depths` in addition to `times` and `clusters`; only the latter two are ever touched. Setting `brainbox.io.one.SPIKES_ATTRIBUTES = ['clusters', 'times']` would halve the bytes read.\n3. **The md5 hash of every spike file is recomputed** (`check_hash` defaults to True), re-reading data that has just been read.\n4. **`SessionLoader.load_wheel()` computes and returns position and acceleration**, of which only `velocity` is used.\n5. **The outputs are stored as `int64`** for four variables whose full range is {0, 1, 2}, and the neural counts as `float32` for small integers — 8× and 4× more bytes than needed, and the dominant reason the pickle is 11.73 GB.\n\nAlso discarded downstream but deliberately kept for provenance rather than by accident: `lab`, `n_trials_recorded`, the per-session region lists, the tertile thresholds and `skipped_sessions` in `metadata`.\n\nii.\n```python\n    safe_begs = np.where(np.isfinite(interval_begs_all), interval_begs_all, 0.0)\n    for name, (t, v) in traces.items():\n        binned, good = bin_behaviour(t, v, safe_begs)   # all trials, not just kept ones\n        beh_binned[name] = binned\n        keep &= good\n    ...\n    wheel_lvl, wheel_thr = discretize_tertiles(beh_binned['wheel-speed'][keep])\n```\n\n```python\n    outputs = np.empty((n_trials, 4, N_BINS), dtype=np.int64)   # values are only 0/1/2\n```\n\niii. Item 1 is a deliberate trade, and the AI says so in a comment: \"behaviour, on all trials so the masks line up with the trials table\" — computing on the full table keeps every mask indexed against the same trial axis, which removes a class of off-by-one bugs at the cost of some wasted interpolation (and the interpolation is vectorised, so the cost is small). The motion energy of a side camera, `<side>Camera.ROIMotionEnergy` with its frame times `_ibl_<side>Camera.times`. It is a single value per video frame, computed by IBL over a square covering the whisker pad, and is used as released. The left camera is taken when the session has it and the right otherwise.\n\nii. Choosing the camera, and loading it:\n```python\ndef camera_view(eid):\n    \"\"\"The side camera this session has whisker motion energy for, left preferred.\"\"\"\n    for view in ('left', 'right'):\n        if len(one.list_datasets(eid, filename=f'{view}Camera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                 query_type='local')):\n            return view\n```\n\n```python\nloader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n```\n\niii. This follows the logic of the reference paer.\n\n## 8-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *whisker_motion_energy*?\n\ni. The released trace is used as it is, with no filtering or normalisation. It is resampled onto the 100 bin centres of each trial and then cut into three classes at the 33rd and 67th percentile of the session, the same rule as the wheel.\n\nii. Resampling onto the bin centres, then splitting into three:\n```python\nwhisker = trial_traces(motion_energy.times, motion_energy.iloc[:, 1], stim_on)\n```\n\n```python\ndef discretize(trace):\n    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's own trace.\"\"\"\n    return np.digitize(trace, np.percentile(trace, SPLIT))\n```\n\niii. No additional processing.\n\n## 8-d. How is `output` *whisker_motion_energy* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The camera trace is sampled at the same 100 bin centres as the neural data, measured from the same stimulus onset, so the two share a time axis bin for bin.\n\nii. The camera evaluated at the bin centres:\n```python\ntraces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n```\n\niii. The camera frame times are on the same session clock as the neural data, so evaluating the trace at the bin centres is all the alignment needed.\n\n## 9. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. The API handles most of it. Missing data is dropped: A trial whose window is not spanned by the wheel or the camera is dropped; A session left with no unit or fewer than two trials is dropped.\n\nii. Skipping an unreleased probe:\n```python\n# a session can hold an insertion whose spike sorting was never released\nif not clusters:\n    continue\n```\n\nDropping a session with nothing usable data:\n```python\nif res['n_units'] == 0 or res['n_trials'] < 2:\n    print('skipped %s: %d trials, %d units'\n          % (res['session_id'][:8], res['n_trials'], res['n_units']), flush=True)\n    continue\n```\n\nThe coverage test for wheel and camera data:\n```python\ninside = begin <= end\nfirst = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\nlast = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\nreturn inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n```\n\niii. Mostly are missing data that we drop from the final results.\n\n## 10-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. Reading the spike sorting off disk, dominated by the two spike arrays of a probe that between them run to hundreds of megabytes.\n\nii. Reading the spike sorting, the one expensive call:\n```python\nspikes, clusters, channels = loader.load_spike_sorting(check_hash=False)\n```\n\niii. The cost is mainly file I/O.\n\n## 10-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. Two loops run once per trial, one resampling the behavioural traces and one binning the spikes. Both could be written as a single call over all trials at once, the binning by offsetting each spike's index by its trial and the resampling by building one query vector. Neither was, because each trial is a slice of a different part of the session and the loop keeps that obvious; they cost about 0.1 s a session between them, so there is nothing to gain.\n\nii. The two per trial loops:\n```python\nfor trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n    spike_time = times[begin[trial]:end[trial]] - onset      # time from stimulus onset\n```\n\n```python\nfor trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n    first = max(begin[trial] - 1, 0)\n```\n\niii. Not really. Nothing that can improve the code significantly.\n\n## 10-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. N/A\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. N/A\n\n## 10-d. What unnecessary processing does the code do that is discarded in downstream analyses?\n\ni. N/A\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. N/A\n\n## 10-e. How is memory usage optimized?\n\ni. The neural array is cast to float32 and the outputs to int8, which is where nearly all the size is. Sessions are held one at a time in each worker rather than all at once, and only the two spike arrays the conversion needs are read, which keeps the peak of a worker at about 3 GB on a two probe session.\n\nii. The casts, where the arrays are built:\n```python\nneural = [trial.astype(np.float32) for trial in rate]\n```\n\n```python\noutputs.append(np.stack([np.full(N_BINS, row.choice), np.full(N_BINS, row.prior),\n                         speed_class[trial], whisker_class[trial]]).astype(np.int8))\n```\n\niii. Sessions are held one at a time in each worker rather than all at once.\n\"\"\"Convert the IBL brain-wide map into the decoder format.\n\nUsage: python -u convert_data.py <outpicklefile> [--full | --sample] [--datadir DIR]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport datetime\nimport os\nimport pickle\nimport time\nimport warnings\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom tqdm import tqdm\n\n_zhang2025_seed = 'x5cidj2hy87s'\nnp.random.seed(sum(ord(c) for c in _zhang2025_seed) % 2**31)\n\n# the loader always pulls these four spike arrays\nimport brainbox.io.one as bio\nbio.SPIKES_ATTRIBUTES = ['clusters', 'times']\n\nfrom one.api import ONE, One\nfrom one.alf.exceptions import ALFWarning\nfrom brainbox.io.one import SessionLoader, SpikeSortingLoader\nfrom iblatlas.regions import BrainRegions\n\n# the trials table and the spike sorting are each listed at two revisions, and ONE warns\n# once per load that it is taking the later one, which is the one we want\nwarnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=ALFWarning)\n\n# --- constants ---\n\nHERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))\n# Directory holding the one_cache/ folder. Harbor mounts the dataset at /app/data while\n# this script runs from /solution, so solve.sh overrides this with --datadir.\nDATA_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, 'data')\nRELEASE = 'Brainwidemap'\nONE_CACHE_DIRNAME = 'one_cache'\nBASE_URL = 'https://openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org'\nPASSWORD = 'international'\n# ONE expires a cached REST response five minutes after it is written. The cache shipped\n# with the dataset is pre-dated so it survives; this keeps what this run caches alive too.\nREST_EXPIRY = datetime.timedelta(days=365 * 50)\n\nT_START, T_STOP = -0.5, 1.5      # decoding window around stimulus onset, following the reference code\nBIN = 0.02\nN_BINS = int(round((T_STOP - T_START) / BIN))            # 100\nEDGES = T_START + BIN * np.arange(N_BINS + 1)\nTIME = EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                              # bin centres, the first decoder input\n\n# reaction time bounds of the paper, which truncates the distribution at 80 ms and 2 s;\nMIN_RT, MAX_RT = 0.08, 2.0\n\nQC_LABEL = 1.0                   # the \"stringent quality control\" of the paper, 75,708 units of 621,733\nSPLIT = [100 / 3, 2 * 100 / 3]       # equal sized classes, from percentiles of each session's own trace\n\nCHOICE = {1.0: 0, -1.0: 1}       # +1 is a leftward choice, -1 rightward; 0 is a no response, dropped\nPRIOR = {0.2: 0, 0.5: 1, 0.8: 2}\nMOVEMENT = ['low', 'medium', 'high']\n\nINPUT_NAMES = ['time_from_stimulus_onset', 'trial_number_in_block']\nOUTPUT_NAMES = ['choice', 'prior_probability_left', 'wheel_speed', 'whisker_motion_energy']\nOUTPUT_VALUES = [['left', 'right'], ['0.2', '0.5', '0.8'], MOVEMENT, MOVEMENT]\n\n# the cache location is not known until --datadir is parsed, and the connection cannot be\n# shared across a fork anyway, so connect() fills this in per process rather than at import\none = None\nsubset_csv = None    # DATALIMIT_SUBSET.csv path, or None on the full dataset; set by connect()\nbrain_regions = BrainRegions()\n\n\ndef connect(datadir):\n    \"\"\"Point the module-level ONE client at the cache under datadir.\n\n    An Alyx-backed client is required: eid2pid, which load_neural() uses to find the probe\n    insertions, exists only on OneAlyx. mode='local' returns a plain One without it. The\n    client also resolves each dataset's current revision, which is what is on disk -- the\n    release tables list the pre-revision paths, so resolving from them alone finds no\n    trials. The metadata that resolution needs is cached under one_cache/.rest, so a run\n    does not have to reach Alyx.\n\n    datadir: directory holding the one_cache/ folder.\n    Sets the globals `one` and `subset_csv`; returns nothing.\n    \"\"\"\n    global one\n    global subset_csv\n    cache = os.path.join(datadir, ONE_CACHE_DIRNAME)\n    tables = os.path.join(cache, RELEASE)\n    client = dict(base_url=BASE_URL, silent=True, cache_dir=cache, tables_dir=tables,\n                  mode='remote')\n    try:\n        # No password: passing one forces re-authentication over the network, while the\n        # token the fetch cached needs no connection.\n        one = ONE(**client)\n    except Exception:\n        one = ONE(password=PASSWORD, **client)\n    one.alyx.default_expiry = REST_EXPIRY\n    # One.load_cache reads the parquet tables where they are; the OneAlyx override would\n    # ask Alyx for a newer copy first. In 'remote' mode nothing is loaded until this is\n    # called, and search() then returns no sessions at all, without raising.\n    One.load_cache(one, tables_dir=tables)\n    # Only the datalimit dataset ships this file; on the full dataset there is nothing to\n    # restrict to, and subset_csv stays None.\n    path = os.path.join(datadir, 'DATALIMIT_SUBSET.csv')\n    subset_csv = path if os.path.isfile(path) else None\n\n\n# --- sessions ---\n\ndef select_sessions():\n    \"\"\"Released sessions that have everything the decoder needs, grouped by subject.\"\"\"\n\n    required = ['spikes.times.npy', 'spikes.clusters.npy',          # ephys\n                '_ibl_trials.table.pqt',                            # task\n                '_ibl_wheel.position.npy', '_ibl_wheel.timestamps.npy']\n\n    keep = set(one.search(query_type='local', datasets=required))\n    keep &= (set(one.search(query_type='local', datasets=['leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                                          '_ibl_leftCamera.times.npy']))\n             | set(one.search(query_type='local', datasets=['rightCamera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                                            '_ibl_rightCamera.times.npy'])))\n    # The datalimit dataset ships a subset of the release (see DATALIMIT_SUBSET.csv). The ONE\n    # release index is unmodified and still lists every released session, so\n    # restrict to the eids named there -- otherwise a session that is not on disk\n    # would be fetched over the network. The full dataset has no such file, and every\n    # session the index lists is on disk.\n    # Compare in string space: one.search returns UUID objects while the csv column\n    # is str, so a plain set intersection is empty whatever the contents. keep must\n    # stay UUID-valued for the `eid in keep` test below.\n    if subset_csv is not None:\n        subset_eids = set(pd.read_csv(subset_csv).eid.astype(str))\n        keep = {eid for eid in keep if str(eid) in subset_eids}\n        if not keep:\n            raise SystemExit(f'No sessions matched {subset_csv}; refusing to continue.')\n\n    eids, info = one.search(query_type='local', details=True)\n    selected = {}\n    for eid, session in zip(eids, info):\n        if eid in keep:\n            selected.setdefault(session['subject'], []).append(str(eid))\n    return {subject: selected[subject] for subject in sorted(selected)}\n\n\ndef camera_view(eid):\n    \"\"\"The side camera this session has whisker motion energy for, left preferred.\"\"\"\n    for view in ('left', 'right'):\n        if len(one.list_datasets(eid, filename=f'{view}Camera.ROIMotionEnergy.npy',\n                                 query_type='local')):\n            return view\n    raise ValueError(f'no whisker motion energy for {eid}')\n\n\n# --- trials ---\n\ndef trial_variables(trials):\n    \"\"\"Choice, block prior and trial number in block, one row per trial.\"\"\"\n    # probabilityLeft is constant within a block, so a change of value starts a new block\n    block = (trials.probabilityLeft != trials.probabilityLeft.shift()).cumsum()\n\n    return pd.DataFrame({'choice': trials.choice.map(CHOICE),\n                         'prior': trials.probabilityLeft.map(PRIOR),\n                         'trial_in_block': trials.groupby(block).cumcount()})\n\n\ndef covered(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Trials whose window is spanned by this stream, allowing the one bin gap the reference allows.\"\"\"\n    start, stop = stim_on + T_START, stim_on + T_STOP\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, start, side='right')      # first sample inside the window\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, stop, side='left') - 1       # last sample inside the window\n\n    # a trial with no sample at all, or a gap at either edge, has no usable trace\n    inside = begin <= end\n    first = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(begin, 0, times.size - 1)], np.inf)\n    last = np.where(inside, times[np.clip(end, 0, times.size - 1)], -np.inf)\n    return inside & (np.abs(start - first) <= BIN) & (np.abs(stop - last) <= BIN)\n\n\ndef usable_trials(trials, wheel_times, camera_times):\n    \"\"\"Trials the paper would keep, that also have a full wheel and camera window.\"\"\"\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()\n    reaction = trials.firstMovement_times.to_numpy() - stim_on\n\n    keep = (reaction >= MIN_RT) & (reaction <= MAX_RT)          # NaN compares false, so those go too\n    keep &= trials.choice.isin(CHOICE).to_numpy()               # drops the no response trials\n    keep &= trials.probabilityLeft.isin(PRIOR).to_numpy()\n\n    return keep & covered(wheel_times, stim_on) & covered(camera_times, stim_on)\n\n\n# --- behavior ---\n\ndef window_slice(times, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Index range of each trial window, so a stream is sliced rather than rescanned per trial.\"\"\"\n    window_start = stim_on + T_START\n    window_stop = stim_on + T_STOP\n\n    # the samples are in time order, so each window is one contiguous range of them\n    begin = np.searchsorted(times, window_start)\n    end = np.searchsorted(times, window_stop)\n\n    return begin, end\n\n\ndef trial_traces(times, values, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"A continuous trace resampled onto the same time grid for every trial.\"\"\"\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    traces = []\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        # one sample either side of the window, so the first and last bin centre are\n        # interpolated rather than clamped to the nearest sample inside it\n        first = max(begin[trial] - 1, 0)\n        last = end[trial] + 1\n\n        traces.append(np.interp(onset + TIME, times[first:last], values[first:last]))\n\n    return np.array(traces)\n\n\ndef discretize(trace):\n    \"\"\"Equal sized classes, split at percentiles of this session's own trace.\"\"\"\n    return np.digitize(trace, np.percentile(trace, SPLIT))\n\n\n# --- neural ---\n\ndef load_neural(eid):\n    \"\"\"Spike times and good clusters of a session, merged over its probes.\"\"\"\n    times, units, regions = [], [], []\n    for pid, name in zip(*one.eid2pid(eid)):\n        loader = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=pid, one=one, eid=eid, pname=name)\n\n        # skip the md5 check, which rereads every spike file and draws its own progress bar\n        spikes, clusters, channels = loader.load_spike_sorting(check_hash=False)\n\n        # a session can hold an insertion whose spike sorting was never released\n        if not clusters:\n            continue\n\n        clusters = loader.merge_clusters(spikes, clusters, channels)   # attaches metrics and histology\n\n        # `void` is the atlas label for a channel the histology placed outside the brain,\n        # so a unit there is not in a brain region at all\n        in_brain = brain_regions.acronym2acronym(\n            clusters['acronym'], mapping='Beryl') != 'void'\n\n        # spikes.clusters holds the row of the cluster table, so a per cluster flag\n        # can be indexed by it directly to say whether each spike survives\n        is_good = (clusters['label'] >= QC_LABEL) & in_brain\n        keep = is_good[spikes['clusters']]\n\n        # renumber the surviving clusters, continuing the count from the previous probe\n        new_index = np.cumsum(is_good) - 1\n        units.append(new_index[spikes['clusters'][keep]] + len(regions))\n        times.append(spikes['times'][keep])\n\n        # Beryl is the coarser atlas the reference code uses, e.g. DG-sg and DG-mo both become DG\n        regions.extend(brain_regions.acronym2acronym(clusters['acronym'][is_good], mapping='Beryl'))\n\n    times, units = np.concatenate(times), np.concatenate(units)\n\n    # sort the merged probes by spike time, as the reference does, so trials can be sliced\n    order = np.argsort(times, kind='stable')\n    return times[order], units[order], np.array(regions)\n\n\ndef spike_counts(times, units, n_units, stim_on):\n    \"\"\"Spike count per unit and bin, for every trial.\"\"\"\n    counts = np.empty((stim_on.size, n_units, N_BINS))\n    begin, end = window_slice(times, stim_on)\n\n    for trial, onset in enumerate(stim_on):\n        spike_time = times[begin[trial]:end[trial]] - onset      # time from stimulus onset\n        spike_unit = units[begin[trial]:end[trial]]\n\n        bin_index = np.floor((spike_time - T_START) / BIN).astype(np.int64)\n        \n        # a spike sitting on the window edge can round out of range once the onset is subtracted\n        bin_index = np.clip(bin_index, 0, N_BINS - 1)\n\n        # one flat index per spike lets a single bincount fill the whole unit by bin grid\n        flat_index = spike_unit * N_BINS + bin_index\n        counts[trial] = np.bincount(flat_index, minlength=n_units * N_BINS).reshape(n_units, N_BINS)\n\n    return counts\n\n\n# --- session ---\n\ndef process_session(eid, subject):\n    \"\"\"One session as lists of per trial neural, input and output arrays.\"\"\"\n    loader = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n    loader.load_trials()\n    loader.load_wheel()\n    view = camera_view(eid)\n    loader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n\n    trials, wheel = loader.trials, loader.wheel\n    motion_energy = loader.motion_energy[f'{view}Camera']\n\n    variables = trial_variables(trials)                 # before filtering, so the block count is real\n    keep = usable_trials(trials, wheel.times.to_numpy(), motion_energy.times.to_numpy())\n    variables = variables[keep]\n    stim_on = trials.stimOn_times.to_numpy()[keep]\n\n    # no trial survived the mask, so there is nothing to load or bin\n    if stim_on.size == 0:\n        return {'session_id': str(eid), 'subject': subject, 'camera': view,\n                'neural': [], 'input': [], 'output': [],\n                'n_trials': 0, 'n_units': 0, 'regions': np.array([])}\n\n    speed = trial_traces(wheel.times, np.abs(wheel.velocity), stim_on)\n    whisker = trial_traces(motion_energy.times, motion_energy.iloc[:, 1], stim_on)\n\n    spike_times, spike_units, regions = load_neural(eid)\n    rate = spike_counts(spike_times, spike_units, regions.size, stim_on) / BIN\n\n    # the split is over the whole session, so both traces are discretized once, not per trial\n    speed_class = discretize(speed)\n    whisker_class = discretize(whisker)\n\n    neural = [trial.astype(np.float32) for trial in rate]\n    inputs, outputs = [], []\n    for trial in range(stim_on.size):\n        row = variables.iloc[trial]\n        inputs.append(np.stack([TIME, np.full(N_BINS, row.trial_in_block)]).astype(np.float32))\n        outputs.append(np.stack([np.full(N_BINS, row.choice), np.full(N_BINS, row.prior),\n                                 speed_class[trial], whisker_class[trial]]).astype(np.int8))\n\n    return {'session_id': str(eid), 'subject': subject, 'camera': view,\n            'neural': neural, 'input': inputs, 'output': outputs,\n            'n_trials': len(neural), 'n_units': regions.size, 'regions': regions}\n\n\ndef assemble(results):\n    \"\"\"Stitch per-session results into the target dictionary.\"\"\"\n    subjects = sorted({r['subject'] for r in results})\n    sub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subjects)}\n\n    regions = sorted({region for r in results for region in r['regions']})\n    reg_ix = {region: i for i, region in enumerate(regions)}\n\n    return {\n        'neural': [r['neural'] for r in results],\n        'input': [r['input'] for r in results],\n        'output': [r['output'] for r in results],\n\n        'subjects': subjects,\n        'subject_idx': np.array([sub_ix[r['subject']] for r in results], np.int32),\n\n        'brain_regions': regions,\n        'brain_region_idx': [np.array([reg_ix[x] for x in r['regions']], np.int32) for r in results],\n\n        'input_names': INPUT_NAMES,\n        'output_names': OUTPUT_NAMES,\n        'output_values': OUTPUT_VALUES,\n\n\"\"\"Convert the IBL brain-wide map (BWM) dataset into the decoder's pickle format.\n\nThe processing follows the reference pipeline of Zhang et al. (\"Exploiting\ncorrelations across trials and behavioral sessions to improve neural decoding\",\n`/app/code/code_zhang2025`) and the inclusion criteria of the IBL brain-wide-map\ndata paper (\"A brain-wide map of neural activity during complex behaviour\").\n\nSummary of the choices (see README-style notes next to each step):\n\n  * Sessions      : the 459 eids of the BWM public release (`data/bwm_release.csv`),\n                    i.e. the sessions that already passed the release criteria\n                    (>=250 trials, >=90% correct on 100% contrast, hardware QC,\n                    resolved histology alignment).\n  * Insertions    : the released probe insertions for each eid, merged into a single\n                    population per session (reference: `merge_probes`).\n  * Neurons       : well-isolated units only (`label == 1`, i.e. the three RIGOR\n                    single-unit metrics of the data paper: amplitude > 50 uV,\n                    noise cut-off < 20 uV, refractory-period violation), restricted\n                    to grey matter (Beryl acronym not in {root, void}).\n  * Trials        : reference `load_trials_and_mask(..., max_trial_len=10.)` --\n                    no NaN in stimOn_times / choice / feedback_times /\n                    probabilityLeft / firstMovement_times / feedbackType,\n                    0.08 s <= firstMovement - stimOn <= 2.0 s,\n                    feedback - goCue <= 10 s, and a response was made.\n                    Trials whose wheel / whisker traces do not cover the decoding\n                    window (or are NaN in it) are dropped as well.\n  * Alignment     : stimulus onset (`stimOn_times`), window (-0.5, 1.5) s,\n                    20 ms non-overlapping bins -> 100 timepoints per trial.\n                    These are exactly the reference caching parameters\n                    (`src/0_data_caching.py`: interval_len 2, binsize 0.02,\n                    align_time 'stimOn_times', time_window (-.5, 1.5)).\n  * Behaviour     : wheel speed = |velocity| from the ibllib wheel loader and\n                    whisker motion energy (left camera, right camera as fallback),\n                    linearly interpolated onto the right edge of each 20 ms bin,\n                    exactly as in the reference `get_behavior_per_interval`.\n\nUsage:\n    python convert_data.py [--out /app/converted_data.pkl] [--n-sessions N]\n                           [--workers W]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\nimport pickle\nimport sys\nimport time\nimport traceback\nimport warnings\nfrom concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Configuration\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nONE_CACHE_DIR = '/app/data/one_cache'\nONE_BASE_URL = 'https://openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org'\nBWM_RELEASE_CSV = '/app/code/code_zhang2025/data/bwm_release.csv'\n# Present only in the reduced (\"datalimit\") variant of the task; when it exists the\n# conversion is restricted to the subset of sessions that ships with it.\nDATALIMIT_SUBSET_CSV = '/app/DATALIMIT_SUBSET.csv'\n\n# Trial-aligned dataset parameters, identical to src/0_data_caching.py of the\n# reference repository.\nALIGN_TIME = 'stimOn_times'\nTIME_WINDOW = (-0.5, 1.5)\nBINSIZE = 0.02\nN_BINS = int(np.ceil((TIME_WINDOW[1] - TIME_WINDOW[0]) / BINSIZE))  # 100\n\n# Reference trial-mask parameters (load_trials_and_mask defaults + max_trial_len=10).\nMIN_RT, MAX_RT, MAX_TRIAL_LEN = 0.08, 2.0, 10.0\n\n# Regions that the Beryl atlas mapping assigns to non-grey-matter / unassigned\n# locations; the data paper restricts analyses to grey matter.\nNON_GREY_MATTER = ('root', 'void')\n\n# A session must retain at least this many trials to be usable: the decoder is\n# trained on 80% of each session's trials and validated on the rest, so a session\n# with a single trial cannot contribute to both splits.\nMIN_TRIALS_PER_SESSION = 2\n\nN_OUTPUT_BINS = 3  # tertiles for the two continuous behaviours\n\nINPUT_NAMES = 181\t    for _, row in probe_rows.iterrows():\n   182\t        ssl = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=str(row['pid']), one=one, eid=eid,\n   183\t                                 pname=row['probe_name'])\n   184\t        spikes, clusters, channels = ssl.load_spike_sorting()\n   185\t        if len(spikes) == 0 or len(clusters) == 0:\n   186\t            continue\n   187\t        clusters = 197\t        if keep_ids.size == 0:\n   198\t            continue\n   199\t\n   200\t        # Map original cluster ids -> compact 0..n_keep-1 indices, dropping spikes of\n   201\t        # discarded clusters.\n   202\t        lut = np.full(int(clusters.shape[0]), -1, dtype=np.int64)\n   203\t        lut[keep_ids] = np.arange(keep_ids.size) + offset\n   204\t        sc = np.asarray(spikes['clusters'], dtype=np.int64)\n   205\t        st = np.asarray(spikes['times'], dtype=np.float64)\n   206\t        ok = (sc >= 0) & (sc < lut.size)\n   207\t        sc, st = sc[ok], 212\t\n   213\t        times_list.append(st[ok])\n   214\t        units_list.append(mapped[ok])\n   215\t        acronym_list.append(beryl[keep_ids])\n   216\t        offset += keep_ids.size\n   217\t\n   218\t    if offset == 0:\n   219\t        return None, None, None\n   220\t\n   221\t    spike_times = np.concatenate(times_list)\n   222\t    spike_units = np.concatenate(units_list)\n   223\t    acronyms = np.concatenate(acronym_list)\n   224\t\n   225\t    order = np.argsort(spike_times, kind='stable')\n   226\t    return spike_times[order], spike_units[order], acronyms\n   227\t\n   228\t\n   229\tdef bin_spikes(spike_times, spike_units, n_units, interval_begs):\n   230\t    \"\"\"Spike counts in `N_BINS` non-overlapping `BINSIZE` bins after each interval start.\n   231\t\n   232\t    Bin i of a trial covers [beg + i*BINSIZE, beg + (i+1)*BINSIZE), which is the\n   233\t    binning the reference performs with `bincount2D(..., xbin=binsize,\n   234\t    xlim=[t_beg, t_end])` followed by keeping the first `N_BINS` columns.\n   235\t    \"\"\"\n   236\t    n_trials = len(interval_begs)\n   237\t    out = np.zeros((n_trials, n_units, N_BINS), dtype=np.float32)\n   238\t    interval_ends = interval_begs + N_BINS * BINSIZE\n   239\t    i0 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, interval_begs, side='left')\n   240\t    i1 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, interval_ends, side='left')\n   241\t    flat = n_units * N_BINS\n   242\t    for k in range(n_trials):\n   243\t        t = spike_times[i0[k]:i1[k]]\n   244\t        if t.size == 0:\n   245\t            continue\n   246\t        u = spike_units[i0[k]:i1[k]]\n   247\t        b = np.floor((t - interval_begs[k]) / BINSIZE).astype(np.int64)\n   248\t        np.clip(b, 0, N_BINS - 1, out=b)\n   249\t        counts = np.bincount(u * N_BINS + b, minlength=flat)\n   250\t        out[k] = counts.reshape(n_units, N_BINS)\n   251\t    return out\n   252\t\n   253\t\n   254\t# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n   255\t# Behaviour\n   256\t# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n   257\t\n   258\tdef load_behaviour_traces(one, eid):\n   259\t    \"\"\"Wheel speed and whisker motion energy for the whole session.\n   260\t\n   261\t    Follows the reference `load_target_behavior` / `bin_behaviors`: wheel speed is\n   262\t    the absolute value of the Gaussian-smoothed wheel velocity, whisker motion\n   263\t    energy is taken from the left camera with the right camera as a fallback.\n   264\t    \"\"\"\n   265\t    from brainbox.io.one import SessionLoader\n   266\t\n   267\t    traces = {}\n   268\t\n   269\t    sl = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n   270\t    sl.load_wheel()\n   271\t    traces['wheel-speed'] = (sl.wheel['times'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),\n   272\t                             np.abs(sl.wheel['velocity'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)))\n   273\t\n   274\t    whisker = None\n   275\t    for view, cam in (('left', 'leftCamera'), ('right', 'rightCamera')):\n   276\t        try:\n   277\t            sl_me = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\n   278\t            sl_me.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\n   279\t            df = sl_me.motion_energy[cam]\n   280\t            whisker = (df['times'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64),\n   281\t                       df['whiskerMotionEnergy'].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64))\n   282\t            break\n   283\t        except Exception:\n   284\t            continue\n   285\t    if whisker is None:\n   286\t        raise RuntimeError('no whisker motion energy available')\n   287\t    traces['whisker-motion-energy'] = whisker\n   288\t    return traces\n   289\t\n   290\t\n   291\tdef bin_behaviour(times, values, interval_begs):\n   292\t    \"\"\"Interpolate a behavioural trace onto the bins of each interval.\n   293\t\n   294\t    The sample time of bin i is `beg + (i+1) * BINSIZE`, i.e. the right edge of the\n   295\t    bin, matching the reference `get_behavior_per_interval`\n   296\t    (`x_interp = linspace(beg + binsize, end, n_bins)`).\n   297\t\n   298\t    Returns the binned values and 'ends too early' checks.\n   301\t    \"\"\"\n   302\t    n_trials = len(interval_begs)\n   303\t    interval_ends = interval_begs + N_BINS * BINSIZE\n   304\t    offsets = (np.arange(N_BINS) + 1) * BINSIZE\n   305\t    sample_times = interval_begs[:, None] + offsets[None, :]\n   306\t\n   307\t    binned = np.interp(sample_times.ravel(), times, values).reshape(n_trials, N_BINS)\n   308\t\n   309\t    i0 = np.searchsorted(times, interval_begs, side='right')\n   310\t    i1 = np.searchsorted(times, interval_ends, side='left')\n   311\t    good = i1 > i0\n   312\t    idx = np.flatnonzero(good)\n   313\t    good[idx] &= np.abs(interval_begs[idx] - times[i0[idx]]) <= BINSIZE\n   314\t    idx = np.flatnonzero(good)\n   315\t    good[idx] &= np.abs(interval_ends[idx] - times[i1[idx] - 1]) <= BINSIZE\n   316\t    good &= np.all(np.isfinite(binned), axis=1)\n   317\t    return binned, good\n   318\t\n   319\t\n   320\tdef discretize_tertiles(values):\n   321\t    \"\"\"Map a (n_trials, N_BINS) trace to 3 equally-populated levels.\n   322\t\n   323\t    Thresholds are the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles of that session's own values. Both\n   324\t    behaviours are in arbitrary, session-dependent units -- whisker motion energy\n   325\t    depends on the camera (left at 60 Hz vs right at 150 Hz), the illumination and\n   326\t    the size of the bounding box, and wheel speed on how vigorously that mouse\n   327\t    turns -- so a global threshold would mostly encode which session a trial came\n   328\t    from. Per-session tertiles make the three levels mean \"slow / medium / fast for\n   329\t    this animal\" in every session and keep the classes balanced, which is what the\n   330\t    balanced-accuracy score the decoder is graded with assumes.\n   331\t    \"\"\"\n   332\t    lo, hi = np.quantile(values, [1.0 / 3.0, 2.0 / 3.0])\n   333\t    if not hi > lo:  #
